subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finsecure.com>
Cc: Ben Torres <ben.torres@finsecure.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — follow-up + next steps

Hi Alice / Ben,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the overview of FinSecure's use cases and the security review you're running. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can get you the material Security needs: 

Recap from call:
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation for production PII-related inference workloads.
- Concern from your security team: egress controls, customer-managed keys, and auditability of model inputs/outputs.
- Current preference: leaning toward Private VPC/on-prem evaluation, but wanted to validate exact differences vs Dedicated Reserved capacity first.

How Redwood maps to the models we discussed:
- Hosted API: best for quick proof-of-concept, not meeting your isolation needs (multi-tenant).
- Dedicated capacity: single-tenant GPU pools with network-level isolation within our cloud provider, private environment options, and optional customer VPC peering for restricted egress paths; good fit for customers who want predictable throughput without full private control plane.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full private control plane, customer-managed networking, optional air-gapped on-prem packaging, customer KMS/HSM integration, and dedicated audit logs — aligns with strict regulatory requirements.

Attachments I'm sharing now:
- SOC2-summary.pdf: short attestation and controls overview
- redwood-dedicated-vs-private-one-pager.pdf: head-to-head feature checklist
- network-requirements.xlsx: typical VPC/on-prem checklist your infra team can use

Next steps (proposed):
1) Can you confirm the must-have vs nice-to-have items for your security team (e.g., must have customer KMS, must have NO outbound internet from serving instances)?
2) If Private is required, would you prefer the Private VPC deployment (Redwood-managed control plane in your VPC) or the on-prem package (air-gapped appliance)?
3) I can set up a technical session with Rishi (solutions engineer) and Neha (security) — are you available Tue/Wed next week?

Thanks,

—Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finsecure.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — follow-up + next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap and the docs — I skimmed SOC2-summary and the one-pager looks useful. High level answers from our InfoSec/Infra teams:

Must-haves:
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM for all keys used to encrypt data at rest and in-flight where applicable.
- No uncontrolled internet egress from serving instances; we need to restrict outbound to a whitelist of endpoints (e.g., logging/metrics endpoints we approve).
- Full audit logs for request inputs and outputs (retention: 1 year) and the ability to export via S3/our SIEM.

Nice-to-haves:
- Ability to run the inference runtime entirely in our VPC under our network controls (VPC peering may be acceptable if egress can be tightly controlled).
- On-prem option if we can't meet the egress/KMS requirements in cloud.

Given the must-haves above, our security team is leaning toward Private VPC or on-prem. We don't want multi-tenant co-located GPUs for production PII workloads. That said, we are open to Dedicated if you can demonstrate: 1) customer KMS integration, 2) strict egress controls (no internet except whitelisted endpoints), and 3) audit/exportable logs.

Can you and your team confirm whether Dedicated meets those three items exactly, or whether Private is mandatory? Also please schedule the technical session — Tue 17th (UTC afternoons) or Wed 18th morning PT works for us.

Best,

Alice Zhang
Head of Security Programs | FinSecure
alice.zhang@finsecure.com

Alice — thanks, super helpful. Looping in Neha (security lead) and Rishi (solutions) so they can confirm specifics and run through a technical checklist in the call. Quick notes before the session: 

- Customer KMS/HSM: Supported in Private (full integration) and supported in Dedicated for keys used to encrypt disks and S3 access; we will confirm whether Dedicated can be configured to use customer-managed HSM for runtime key ops (Rishi will validate).
- Egress controls: Dedicated supports VPC peering + egress ACLs at the subnet level; Private supports placing runtime in your VPC with strict route tables and no internet gateway. We need to validate allowed outbound endpoints for metrics/logging and whether we can push logs directly into your S3.
- Audit logs: We provide request/response logging for both Dedicated and Private; retention and exportability are configurable. On Private you get more direct control over retention and routing.

Rishi/Neha — could you confirm: 1) whether Dedicated can be configured to use customer HSM for runtime ops (or if that requires a Private deployment), and 2) what exact egress locking options we can offer for Dedicated next week on the call?

I'll send a calendar invite for Tue 17th 17:00 UTC / Wed 18th 09:00 PT (per Alice availability) unless you propose another time.

Thanks,

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — follow-up + next steps

Hi Alice / team,

Quick technical summary ahead of tomorrow's session: 

1) Customer KMS/HSM:
- Private: full support for customer-managed KMS/HSM for both disk and runtime keying; we can integrate with your HSM or use customer KMS in your cloud account.
- Dedicated: supports customer-managed KMS for storage (EBS/S3) and secrets; runtime HSM for ephemeral model keys is currently available only with Private deployments. If runtime HSM is a hard requirement, Private is the safer path.

2) Egress controls / network:
- Dedicated: we can deploy Dedicated pools into a customer VPC via VPC peering and enforce strict subnet route tables and NAT/egress gateways. Outbound can be limited to whitelisted endpoints (metrics, selected logging endpoints). There are a few managed control plane callbacks to Redwood for health checks and billing; we can discuss the exact endpoints and scope during the call.
- Private: runtime resides fully in your VPC / on-prem with no mandatory callbacks to Redwood (can be configured for offline operation).

3) Audit logs and export:
- Both modes can produce request/response logs. Dedicated stores logs in a managed bucket by default but can forward to your S3/SIEM. Private gives you direct control over log storage and retention policies. Retention 1 year is supported via configuration in both modes.

Recommendation: from a security guarantee perspective, if your security team requires runtime HSM and zero mandatory control-plane callbacks, Private (VPC or on-prem) is the recommended path. If runtime HSM is optional and your infra team is comfortable with tightly-controlled VPC peering and whitelisted egress, Dedicated is potentially acceptable and offers faster time-to-prod.

I'll bring configuration artifacts and the network-requirements.xlsx to the call and be prepared to walk through the specific endpoints we need to allow.

—Rishi
